sources.read_version: arXiv v1, 4 October 2026, 65 pages; Theorems 1.1–1.3, Sections 1.1.1, 4.1–4.2; selected statements and proof route checked, not a full proof audit
sources.annotation: Pelagic Fourier Fishing gives an optimal one-query bounded-error versus linear randomized query separation for a total relation, via a two-way communication lower bound. Fourier sampling lands in the middle of squared Fourier mass with probability at least 3/4; the classical proof uses entropy/coupling and a Gaussian window robust to shifts. The exact protocol of Theorem 1.3 is a different communication problem and yields a fixed-degree polynomial, not exponential, separation. No exact query separation is inferred from it.

measures.name: deterministic parity query complexity
measures.definition: Minimum worst-case number of queries, each returning the parity over F_2 of a chosen subset of input bits, sufficient to output a valid answer deterministically on every promised input.

aliases.normalization: An entire parity query costs one. These are different measures from bit-query complexity.

measures.notes: The queried subset can depend on previous parity answers unless nonadaptivity is explicitly imposed.

measures.name: bounded-error randomized parity query complexity
measures.definition: Minimum worst-case number of queries, each returning the parity over F_2 of a chosen subset of input bits, sufficient to output a valid answer with probability at least 2/3 on every promised input.

aliases.normalization: An entire parity query costs one. These are different measures from bit-query complexity.

measures.notes: The queried subset can depend on previous parity answers unless nonadaptivity is explicitly imposed.

measures.name: pseudo-deterministic randomized parity query complexity
measures.definition: Minimum worst-case number of queries, each returning the parity over F_2 of a chosen subset of input bits, sufficient to output one fixed valid selector with probability at least 2/3 on every promised input.

aliases.normalization: An entire parity query costs one. These are different measures from bit-query complexity.

measures.notes: The queried subset can depend on previous parity answers unless nonadaptivity is explicitly imposed.

measures.name: deterministic positive AND/OR query complexity
measures.definition: Minimum worst-case query cap when each query is either a conjunction or a disjunction of a chosen subset of non-negated input variables. The algorithm is deterministic and returns a valid output.

aliases.normalization: Both subset queries cost one; do not identify with bit queries or conjunctions of arbitrary signed literals.

measures.notes: Both subset queries cost one; do not identify with bit queries or conjunctions of arbitrary signed literals.

measures.name: bounded-error randomized positive AND/OR query complexity
measures.definition: Minimum worst-case query cap when each query is either a conjunction or a disjunction of a chosen subset of non-negated input variables. On every promised input it returns a valid answer with probability at least 2/3.

aliases.normalization: Both subset queries cost one; do not identify with bit queries or conjunctions of arbitrary signed literals.

measures.notes: Both subset queries cost one; do not identify with bit queries or conjunctions of arbitrary signed literals.

measures.name: pseudo-deterministic randomized positive AND/OR query complexity
measures.definition: Minimum worst-case query cap when each query is either a conjunction or a disjunction of a chosen subset of non-negated input variables. On every promised input it returns one fixed valid selector value with probability at least 2/3.

aliases.normalization: Both subset queries cost one; do not identify with bit queries or conjunctions of arbitrary signed literals.

measures.notes: Both subset queries cost one; do not identify with bit queries or conjunctions of arbitrary signed literals.

measures.name: deterministic zero-answer depth
measures.definition: Minimum over correct deterministic bit-query trees of the maximum number of edges labelled zero on a root-to-leaf path. Edges labelled one cost zero.

aliases.normalization: Zero-answer cost, not zero-error randomized complexity.
Deterministic count of zero answers; not a zero-error randomized measure.
Zero-answer depth and positive-conjunction depth for search relations. The subscript 0 is a cost convention, not an error probability.

measures.notes: Zero-answer cost, not zero-error randomized complexity.

measures.name: randomized zero-answer depth
measures.definition: Minimum worst-support zero-answer depth of a randomized bit-query tree correct with probability at least 1-epsilon on every input. Epsilon=1/3 unless specified.

aliases.normalization: Counts zero answers along paths; NOT R0, the expected cost of a zero-error algorithm.

measures.notes: Counts zero answers along paths; NOT R0, the expected cost of a zero-error algorithm.

measures.name: randomized decision tree rank
measures.definition: Minimum over bounded-error randomized trees of the maximum Strahler rank of any deterministic tree in the support. Error is 1/3 on each input.

aliases.normalization: Support maximum, not expected rank; deterministic rank is DTRank.
Strahler rank; randomized rank takes the maximum rank in the support.

measures.notes: Support maximum, not expected rank; deterministic rank is DTRank.

measures.name: 0-monochromatic subcube cover number
measures.definition: Minimum number of 0-monochromatic subcubes whose union is f^{-1}(0).

aliases.normalization: Counts subcubes, not certificate width; zero for an empty output fibre.

measures.notes: Counts subcubes, not certificate width; zero for an empty output fibre.

measures.name: 1-monochromatic subcube cover number
measures.definition: Minimum number of 1-monochromatic subcubes whose union is f^{-1}(1).

aliases.normalization: Counts subcubes, not certificate width; zero for an empty output fibre.

measures.notes: Counts subcubes, not certificate width; zero for an empty output fibre.

measures.name: monochromatic subcube cover number
measures.definition: The sum N_0(f)+N_1(f) of the two monochromatic subcube cover numbers.

aliases.normalization: Unbounded counts are distinct from certificate widths and logarithms of cover counts.

measures.notes: Unbounded counts are distinct from certificate widths and logarithms of cover counts.

measures.name: average-cost deterministic query complexity
measures.definition: Minimum expected query count E_{x~mu} cost(T,x) over deterministic trees correct on every promised input.
measures.notes: The distribution mu is fixed and known in this nonuniform query model. This is not Ddist, which budgets average error instead of averaging cost. Display symbol is repository notation, not a verified literal source occurrence.

measures.name: average-cost bounded-error randomized query complexity
measures.definition: Minimum E_{x~mu,coins} cost(A,x) over randomized solvers with probability at least 2/3 of a valid answer on every promised input.
measures.notes: The distribution mu is fixed and known in this nonuniform query model. This is not Ddist, which budgets average error instead of averaging cost. Display symbol is repository notation, not a verified literal source occurrence.

measures.name: average-cost strict Las Vegas query complexity
measures.definition: Minimum E_{x~mu,coins} cost(A,x) over randomized algorithms that terminate and return a valid answer with probability one on every promised input.
measures.notes: The distribution mu is fixed and known in this nonuniform query model. This is not Ddist, which budgets average error instead of averaging cost. Display symbol is repository notation, not a verified literal source occurrence.

measures.name: average-cost pseudo-deterministic query complexity
measures.definition: Minimum E_{x~mu,coins} cost(A,x) over algorithms with one fixed valid selector value returned with probability at least 2/3 on every promised input.
measures.notes: The distribution mu is fixed and known in this nonuniform query model. This is not Ddist, which budgets average error instead of averaging cost. Display symbol is repository notation, not a verified literal source occurrence.

measures.name: average-cost strict canonical zero-error query complexity
measures.definition: Minimum over valid selectors g of R0avg_mu(g); equivalently, an almost-surely terminating randomized algorithm must output the same g(x) with probability one on every input.
measures.notes: The distribution mu is fixed and known in this nonuniform query model. This is not Ddist, which budgets average error instead of averaging cost. Display symbol is repository notation, not a verified literal source occurrence.

measures.name: zero-error randomized query cap with detectable failure
measures.definition: Minimum worst-case query cap of a randomized search algorithm that never outputs an invalid answer, but may output the failure symbol bottom with probability at most 1/3 on each input.
measures.notes: A failure flag is permitted. R0 instead requires eventual valid output and uses expected cost. The displayed symbol is a repository scalar label. Display symbol is repository notation, not a verified literal source occurrence.

measures.name: deterministic decision tree total-node size
measures.definition: Minimum total number of nodes, including leaves and internal nodes, of a correct full binary bit-query tree.

aliases.normalization: CMP22 counts nodes; CDM23/CDMRS23 count leaves. For full binary trees DTNodes=2 DTSize(repository leaf count)-1. Do not use the same source typography to assert identical normalizations.

measures.notes: CMP22 counts nodes; CDM23/CDMRS23 count leaves. For full binary trees DTNodes=2 DTSize(repository leaf count)-1. Do not use the same source typography to assert identical normalizations.

measures.name: randomized decision tree total-node size
measures.definition: Minimum worst-support total-node count of a randomized bit-query tree correct with probability at least 2/3 on each input.

aliases.normalization: Whole-node count, not leaf count or expected size. RNodes=2 RSize-1 under full binary tree conventions.

measures.notes: Whole-node count, not leaf count or expected size. RNodes=2 RSize-1 under full binary tree conventions.

measures.name: error-parameter quantum search query complexity
measures.definition: Minimum quantum bit-query cap with probability at least 1-epsilon of outputting some valid answer on every promised input.

aliases.normalization: CMP22 uses epsilon=2/5 for randomized-tree simulations. Arbitrary relations do not automatically admit majority error reduction; this is separate from decision Q_eps and default search Q at error 1/3.

measures.notes: CMP22 uses epsilon=2/5 for randomized-tree simulations. Arbitrary relations do not automatically admit majority error reduction; this is separate from decision Q_eps and default search Q at error 1/3.

measures.name: minimum deterministic tree guessing complexity
measures.definition: Minimum over correct deterministic trees T of G(T), where G(T) minimizes the largest number of red edges on a path over edge colorings having at most one black child edge at each node.

aliases.normalization: The source defines G(T) for a tree; this catalogue additionally minimizes it over valid trees. Claim 12 identifies tree guessing complexity with tree Strahler rank. No new source notation G(f) is asserted. Printed G(T), not the repository function-level minimum.

measures.notes: The source defines G(T) for a tree; this catalogue additionally minimizes it over valid trees. Claim 12 identifies tree guessing complexity with tree Strahler rank. No new source notation G(f) is asserted.

measures.name: bomb query complexity
measures.definition: Minimum bomb-query cap with explosion probability at most 0.01 and total error (including explosion) at most 0.01 on every promised input. A bomb query uses a controlled input query with a clean zero record bit, measures it immediately, and terminates on outcome one.

aliases.normalization: Fixed error constants; the source shorthand B is used only up to its constant-error equivalence.

measures.notes: Fixed error constants; the source shorthand B is used only up to its constant-error equivalence.

measures.name: error-parameter bomb query complexity
measures.definition: Minimum number of controlled queries in the bomb model with explosion probability at most epsilon and total error, including explosion, at most delta on every promised input. The record starts at zero and is measured immediately after each query; outcome one terminates the algorithm.

aliases.normalization: Both error budgets are explicit; 0<epsilon<=delta in the usual regime. The source total-error requirement is not error conditioned on survival.

measures.notes: Both error budgets are explicit; 0<epsilon<=delta in the usual regime. The source total-error requirement is not error conditioned on survival.

measures.name: real multilinear monomial sparsity on the 0/1 cube
measures.definition: Number of nonzero coefficients in the unique representation f(x)=sum_{S subset [n]} a_S product_{i in S} x_i on {0,1}^n, including the empty monomial.

aliases.normalization: The 0/1 monomial basis, not the Walsh Fourier basis. KLMY21 separately uses Fourier sparsity when discussing XOR-functions.

measures.notes: For AND_n this sparsity is 1, while every Walsh Fourier coefficient is nonzero. Logarithmic bounds are interpreted with log(2+spar) at the constant-size boundary.

measures.name: approximate real monomial sparsity
measures.definition: Minimum number of nonzero coefficients in the 0/1 multilinear monomial representation of a real polynomial p with |p(x)-f(x)|<=1/3 on every Boolean input.

aliases.normalization: Approximation on the full cube and sparsity in the 0/1 monomial basis, not Walsh approximate Fourier sparsity.

measures.notes: Kept separate from exact monomial sparsity and Fourier sparsity.

measures.name: real monomial coefficient weight
measures.definition: Sum of absolute coefficients of the unique multilinear real polynomial equal to f on the full Boolean cube, in the 0/1 monomial basis.
measures.notes: Total Boolean functions; signed coefficients. Generalized representations are not conical nonnegative representations.

measures.name: approximate real monomial coefficient weight
measures.definition: Minimum sum of absolute coefficients of a real multilinear 0/1 monomial polynomial that pointwise approximates f within 1/3 on the full cube.
measures.notes: Total Boolean functions; signed coefficients. Generalized representations are not conical nonnegative representations.

measures.name: generalized real monomial sparsity
measures.definition: Minimum number of nonzero signed real coefficients representing f exactly as a linear combination of subcube indicators product_{i in S} x_i product_{j in T}(1-x_j), with S and T disjoint.
measures.notes: Total Boolean functions; signed coefficients. Generalized representations are not conical nonnegative representations.

measures.name: approximate generalized real monomial sparsity
measures.definition: Minimum number of nonzero signed real coefficients in a linear combination of subcube indicators approximating f pointwise within 1/3 on the full cube.
measures.notes: Total Boolean functions; signed coefficients. Generalized representations are not conical nonnegative representations.

measures.name: generalized real monomial coefficient weight
measures.definition: Minimum sum of absolute signed real coefficients among exact representations of f by subcube indicators. The dictionary is redundant; minimize over representations.
measures.notes: Total Boolean functions; signed coefficients. Generalized representations are not conical nonnegative representations.

measures.name: approximate generalized real monomial coefficient weight
measures.definition: Minimum sum of absolute signed real coefficients among subcube-indicator representations approximating f pointwise within 1/3 on the full cube.
measures.notes: Total Boolean functions; signed coefficients. Generalized representations are not conical nonnegative representations.

measures.name: Nisan expected two-sided-error randomized query complexity
measures.definition: Minimum worst-case expected number of queries of an always-terminating randomized decision tree with error at most 1/4 on every input.

measures.name: Nisan expected one-sided-error randomized query complexity
measures.definition: Minimum worst-case expected queries; always reject 0-inputs and accept 1-inputs with probability at least 1/2.

measures.name: permutation decision-tree depth
measures.definition: Minimum worst-case number of queries pi(i)=? or pi^{-1}(j)=? computing f:S_n->{0,1}; each query returns a symbol in [n].
measures.journal_definition_check: Final journal Section 2.2; forward/inverse query family, packing sensitivity and detectable failure 2/3 preserved.

measures.name: permutation polynomial degree
measures.definition: Minimum degree of a real polynomial in permutation-matrix entries agreeing with f on S_n. Equivalently, span of functions depending on at most d values pi(i).
measures.journal_definition_check: Final journal Section 2.2; forward/inverse query family, packing sensitivity and detectable failure 2/3 preserved.

measures.name: permutation approximate degree
measures.definition: Minimum degree of a real polynomial in permutation-matrix entries approximating f within 1/3 on S_n.
measures.journal_definition_check: Final journal Section 2.2; forward/inverse query family, packing sensitivity and detectable failure 2/3 preserved.

measures.name: disjoint-transposition sensitivity
measures.definition: Maximum over pi of the largest family of pairwise disjoint transpositions tau with f(tau*pi)!=f(pi).
measures.journal_definition_check: Final journal Section 2.2; forward/inverse query family, packing sensitivity and detectable failure 2/3 preserved.

measures.name: transposition edge sensitivity
measures.definition: Maximum over pi of the total number of transpositions tau with f(pi*tau)!=f(pi); disjointness is not required.
measures.journal_definition_check: Final journal Section 2.2; forward/inverse query family, packing sensitivity and detectable failure 2/3 preserved.

measures.name: permutation block sensitivity
measures.definition: Maximum over pi of the largest family of permutations tau_j with pairwise disjoint moved-point supports and f(tau_j*pi)!=f(pi).
measures.journal_definition_check: Final journal Section 2.2; forward/inverse query family, packing sensitivity and detectable failure 2/3 preserved.

measures.name: exit-sensitive sensitivity
measures.definition: Maximum over promised x of the number of single-bit flips yielding the opposite output OR leaving the promise.

measures.name: exit-sensitive block sensitivity
measures.definition: Maximum over promised x of the number of pairwise disjoint blocks whose flip yields the opposite output OR leaves the promise.

measures.name: completion-critical block sensitivity
measures.definition: Minimum over total Boolean completions F of max_{x in Dom(f)} bs(F,x). Off-promise inputs are excluded from the outer maximum, but blocks may lead to them.

measures.name: block-optimal-completion critical certificate complexity
measures.definition: Among total completions F attaining completion-critical block sensitivity, minimize max_{x in Dom(f)} C(F,x). The minimization is constrained to block-optimal completions.

measures.name: permutation certificate complexity
measures.definition: Maximum over pi of the minimum number of specified permutation entries whose presence forces f(pi) on S_n.
measures.notes: Not the Boolean-cube measure. In particular R_0 here is a capped detectable-failure model with failure 2/3, not expected Las Vegas cost.
measures.journal_definition_check: Final journal Section 2.2; forward/inverse query family, packing sensitivity and detectable failure 2/3 preserved.

measures.name: permutation unambiguous certificate complexity

measures.journal_definition_check: Final journal Section 2.2; forward/inverse query family, packing sensitivity and detectable failure 2/3 preserved.

measures.name: permutation fractional block sensitivity
measures.definition: At pi, maximize the total nonnegative weight on opposite-output permutations, with total weight at most one for each removed entry of pi. Maximize over pi.
measures.notes: Not the Boolean-cube measure. In particular R_0 here is a capped detectable-failure model with failure 2/3, not expected Las Vegas cost.
measures.journal_definition_check: Final journal Section 2.2; forward/inverse query family, packing sensitivity and detectable failure 2/3 preserved.

measures.name: permutation randomized query depth

measures.name: query-domain deterministic depth
measures.definition: Minimum depth of a decision tree whose query Q returns the unique element of x intersect Q, for x in X.
measures.notes: Domain X consists of n-element subsets of U. Each allowed query intersects every input in exactly one element, and queries cover U. Use domain-qualified scopes; this is not an additional Boolean-cube definition.
measures.journal_definition_check: Final journal Section 2.2; forward/inverse query family, packing sensitivity and detectable failure 2/3 preserved.

measures.name: query-domain bounded-error randomized depth
measures.definition: Minimum common depth cap of a distribution over domain decision trees, with success at least 2/3 on each x in X.
measures.notes: Domain X consists of n-element subsets of U. Each allowed query intersects every input in exactly one element, and queries cover U. Use domain-qualified scopes; this is not an additional Boolean-cube definition.
measures.journal_definition_check: Final journal Section 2.2; forward/inverse query family, packing sensitivity and detectable failure 2/3 preserved.

measures.name: query-domain detectable-failure depth
measures.definition: Minimum common depth cap of zero-error trees with outputs 0,1,star and failure probability at most 2/3 on every x.
measures.notes: Domain X consists of n-element subsets of U. Each allowed query intersects every input in exactly one element, and queries cover U. Use domain-qualified scopes; this is not an additional Boolean-cube definition.
measures.journal_definition_check: Final journal Section 2.2; forward/inverse query family, packing sensitivity and detectable failure 2/3 preserved.

measures.name: query-domain bounded-error quantum queries
measures.definition: Minimum coherent domain-symbol oracle queries computing the Boolean output with error at most 1/3.
measures.notes: Domain X consists of n-element subsets of U. Each allowed query intersects every input in exactly one element, and queries cover U. Use domain-qualified scopes; this is not an additional Boolean-cube definition.
measures.journal_definition_check: Final journal Section 2.2; forward/inverse query family, packing sensitivity and detectable failure 2/3 preserved.

measures.name: query-domain exact quantum queries
measures.definition: Minimum fixed coherent domain-symbol oracle query count computing the output with certainty.
measures.notes: Domain X consists of n-element subsets of U. Each allowed query intersects every input in exactly one element, and queries cover U. Use domain-qualified scopes; this is not an additional Boolean-cube definition.
measures.journal_definition_check: Final journal Section 2.2; forward/inverse query family, packing sensitivity and detectable failure 2/3 preserved.

measures.name: query-domain spatial degree
measures.definition: Minimum maximum |A| in a linear combination of indicators [A subseteq x] representing f on X; equivalently degree in membership indicators.
measures.notes: Domain X consists of n-element subsets of U. Each allowed query intersects every input in exactly one element, and queries cover U. Use domain-qualified scopes; this is not an additional Boolean-cube definition.
measures.journal_definition_check: Final journal Section 2.2; forward/inverse query family, packing sensitivity and detectable failure 2/3 preserved.

measures.name: query-domain spatial approximate degree
measures.definition: Minimum maximum |A| in a real linear combination of indicators [A subseteq x] approximating f within 1/3 on X. No bound outside X is imposed.
measures.notes: Domain X consists of n-element subsets of U. Each allowed query intersects every input in exactly one element, and queries cover U. Use domain-qualified scopes; this is not an additional Boolean-cube definition.
measures.journal_definition_check: Final journal Section 2.2; forward/inverse query family, packing sensitivity and detectable failure 2/3 preserved.

measures.name: query-domain certificate complexity
measures.definition: Maximum over x in X of the minimum |a| for a subset a of x such that every y in X extending a has f(y)=f(x).
measures.notes: Domain X consists of n-element subsets of U. Each allowed query intersects every input in exactly one element, and queries cover U. Use domain-qualified scopes; this is not an additional Boolean-cube definition.
measures.journal_definition_check: Final journal Section 2.2; forward/inverse query family, packing sensitivity and detectable failure 2/3 preserved.

measures.name: query-domain unambiguous certificate complexity
measures.definition: Minimum largest certificate size in a collection of subsets of the universe such that every x in X extends exactly one certificate.
measures.notes: Domain X consists of n-element subsets of U. Each allowed query intersects every input in exactly one element, and queries cover U. Use domain-qualified scopes; this is not an additional Boolean-cube definition.
measures.journal_definition_check: Final journal Section 2.2; forward/inverse query family, packing sensitivity and detectable failure 2/3 preserved.

measures.name: query-domain block sensitivity
measures.definition: Maximum over x of the largest family of opposite-output y_j in X for which the removed-entry sets x minus y_j are pairwise disjoint.
measures.notes: Domain X consists of n-element subsets of U. Each allowed query intersects every input in exactly one element, and queries cover U. Use domain-qualified scopes; this is not an additional Boolean-cube definition.
measures.journal_definition_check: Final journal Section 2.2; forward/inverse query family, packing sensitivity and detectable failure 2/3 preserved.

measures.name: query-domain fractional block sensitivity
measures.definition: Maximum over x of the nonnegative weighted packing of opposite-output y, subject to total weight at most one through each removed element of x.
measures.notes: Domain X consists of n-element subsets of U. Each allowed query intersects every input in exactly one element, and queries cover U. Use domain-qualified scopes; this is not an additional Boolean-cube definition.
measures.journal_definition_check: Final journal Section 2.2; forward/inverse query family, packing sensitivity and detectable failure 2/3 preserved.

measures.name: query-domain chunk sensitivity
measures.definition: Maximum over x of the largest family of opposite-output y_j with pairwise disjoint x minus y_j and each |x minus y_j| equal to the domain chunk size c.

aliases.normalization: Packing sensitivity for disjoint sensitive two-coordinate blocks on a single multislice; equals domain chunk sensitivity there.

measures.notes: Domain X consists of n-element subsets of U. Each allowed query intersects every input in exactly one element, and queries cover U. Use domain-qualified scopes; this is not an additional Boolean-cube definition.
measures.journal_definition_check: Final journal Section 2.2; forward/inverse query family, packing sensitivity and detectable failure 2/3 preserved.

measures.name: covering radius of a promise domain
measures.definition: For nonempty X=Dom(f) subseteq {+1,-1}^n, max over cube points y of min_{x in X} HammingDistance(x,y).
measures.notes: These are domain/polynomial parameters, not canonical Fourier statistics of an incompletely defined Boolean function.

measures.name: coordinate Fourier sparsity of a fixed polynomial
measures.definition: Number of nonzero Walsh Fourier coefficients of p whose index sets contain the specified coordinate i.
measures.notes: These are domain/polynomial parameters, not canonical Fourier statistics of an incompletely defined Boolean function.

measures.name: coordinate Fourier influence of a fixed polynomial
measures.definition: E[(D_i p)^2] under the uniform full cube, where D_i p(x)=(p(x)-p(x^i))/2; equals sum_{S containing i} p_hat(S)^2.
measures.notes: These are domain/polynomial parameters, not canonical Fourier statistics of an incompletely defined Boolean function.

measures.name: maximum coordinate derivative sup norm
measures.definition: Maximum over i and full-cube x of |p(x)-p(x^i)|/2 for a fixed polynomial p.
measures.notes: These are domain/polynomial parameters, not canonical Fourier statistics of an incompletely defined Boolean function. The maximum is an equivalent repository aggregation of the source’s bounds for every coordinate; its literal displayed name is not verified.

measures.name: distributional bit-flip squared influence
measures.definition: E_{X drawn from lambda}[(p(X)-p(X flipped at i))^2] for a function p on the entire Boolean cube. The off-support value is used even if lambda is a slice distribution.

aliases.normalization: Uniform cube; unnormalized squared flip difference. Equals four times the HKMP26 derivative-normalized influence for the same full-cube function.

measures.notes: Distribution/coordinate parameters stay explicit. This is an averaged squared difference, not maximum disjoint-transposition sensitivity.

measures.name: distributional total bit-flip squared influence
measures.definition: Sum over coordinates i of E_lambda[(p(X)-p(X flipped at i))^2] for a full-cube function p.
measures.notes: Distribution/coordinate parameters stay explicit. This is an averaged squared difference, not maximum disjoint-transposition sensitivity.

measures.name: distributional variance
measures.definition: E_lambda[(p(X)-E_lambda p)^2] for a full-cube function p; only its restriction to the support is needed for variance.
measures.notes: Distribution/coordinate parameters stay explicit. This is an averaged squared difference, not maximum disjoint-transposition sensitivity.

measures.name: slice transposition squared influence
measures.definition: E over the uniform k-slice of (p(X)-p(X with coordinates i,j swapped))^2. This depends only on values on the slice.
measures.notes: Distribution/coordinate parameters stay explicit. This is an averaged squared difference, not maximum disjoint-transposition sensitivity.

measures.name: degree-optimal bounded exact Fourier sparsity of a partial function
measures.definition: Minimum number of nonzero Walsh coefficients among full-cube [-1,1]-bounded polynomials representing the ±1-valued partial function exactly on its promise, constrained to have minimum possible globally bounded exact degree.
measures.notes: Keep degree optimality, the basis, output encoding and bias convention explicit. These are not ordinary unconstrained approximate monomial sparsity.

measures.name: degree-optimal bounded approximate Fourier sparsity of a partial function
measures.definition: Minimum number of nonzero Walsh coefficients among full-cube [-1,1]-bounded polynomials approximating the ±1-valued partial function within 1/3 on its promise, constrained to have minimum possible bounded approximate degree at that error.
measures.notes: Keep degree optimality, the basis, output encoding and bias convention explicit. These are not ordinary unconstrained approximate monomial sparsity.

measures.name: biased Fourier coefficient influence
measures.definition: Sum of squared p-biased orthonormal Fourier coefficients indexed by sets containing i. HKMP26 uses p=Pr[x_i=-1], mean mu=1-2p and sigma=2*sqrt(p*(1-p)). This equals sigma^2*E_p[(D_i f)^2].
measures.notes: Keep degree optimality, the basis, output encoding and bias convention explicit. These are not ordinary unconstrained approximate monomial sparsity.

claims.statement: For partial Boolean functions, cubeBoundedDeg=O(log N) while Q=tildeOmega(N^(1/3)); no finite polynomial in cubeBoundedDeg upper-bounds Q.
claims.locator: Corollary 2, Theorems 1, 6 and 8; definition in Section 2.1
claims.proof_summary: Construct threshold satisfiability with a degree-nine globally bounded representing polynomial over a large alphabet. Prove a quantum lower bound for the contained tripartite shift problem using a negative-weight adversary; encode alphabet symbols in O(log N) bits.

claims.statement: Extremal Forrelation has QE=1 in the paper’s joint phase-oracle convention and R=tildeOmega(N^(1/4)), for truth-table input length N=2^(n+1). A standard bit-oracle convention changes the quantum cost by at most a constant.
claims.proof_summary: One interference experiment determines the sign when the forrelation is promised to be exactly plus or minus one. For the classical lower bound, construct bent-function instances and use a linear-algebraic analysis of limited transcripts.

claims.statement: Adv(S)<=CAdv(S).
claims.proof_summary: Use sqrt(ab)>=min(a,b) in each disjoint-valid-output constraint.

claims.statement: fbs(S)<=CAdv(S).
claims.proof_summary: For a fixed input, the classical-adversary weights form a feasible fractional certificate against inputs with disjoint valid-output sets.

claims.statement: bs(S)<=fbs(S).
claims.proof_summary: Assign unit weight to a packing of pairwise disjoint sensitive blocks.

claims.statement: fcbs(S)<=2 CAdv(S).
claims.proof_summary: Choose a valid-output selector using a weighted nearest critical input, then double the critical input weights to construct its fractional certificate.

claims.statement: CAdv(S)<=2 Adv(S)^2.
claims.proof_summary: The partial-function Cauchy–Schwarz proof of ABK21 Theorem 30 uses only constrained pairs, so it extends to disjoint valid-output sets.

claims.statement: fcbs(S)=O(rel_adeg(S)^2) at fixed error below 1/2.
claims.proof_summary: Choose the largest valid-output polynomial as selector. At a critical input its polynomial exceeds one half; reduce to the partial one-versus-rest problem and apply the bounded-polynomial fractional-sensitivity bound.

claims.statement: fbs(S)=O(rel_adeg(S)^2) at fixed error below 1/2.
claims.proof_summary: At a fixed input, sum the polynomial mass over its valid outputs. On every disjoint-output input the mass is small, yielding a bounded polynomial for a partial decision problem.

claims.statement: Adv(S)=O(Q(S)).
claims.proof_summary: Apply the positive adversary progress argument only to inputs whose valid-output sets are disjoint.

claims.statement: CAdv(S)=O(R(S)).
claims.proof_summary: A randomized solver distinguishes inputs with disjoint valid-output sets; its query weights satisfy the adversary constraints after constant rescaling.

claims.statement: For the total pigeonhole search problem PH_n, CAdv<=2 log(n/2) but rel_adeg=tildeOmega(n^(1/3)). Thus no finite power of CAdv, or of positive Adv, upper-bounds relation approximate degree.
claims.proof_summary: Any two inputs with disjoint collision certificates differ in at least n/2 bits, so uniform weights give a logarithmic classical adversary. Symmetrize the output-polynomial system and reduce to the collision lower bound.
claims.notes: Collision certificates include both colliding indices and their shared values. Do not apply the decision-function inequality Adv=O(approximate-degree^2) in the reverse direction, or confuse relation polynomial systems with a single polynomial.

claims.statement: BK24 constructs partial decision functions with bounded approximate degree and two-sided conical degree O(polylog n), but Q=tildeOmega(n^(1/6)); input length is at most 2^polylog(n).
claims.proof_summary: Index an auxiliary bit y_c by every solution certificate c. Promise that all bits y_c for certificates valid on x have the same value, and ask for that value. Polynomial systems transfer via sum_c p_c(x)y_c. In the reverse direction, measure a decision algorithm’s query register on auxiliary input all zero and verify sampled certificates. The quantum hybrid argument gives Q(search)<=tildeO(Q(decision)^3), hence the cube-root lower-bound transfer.

claims.statement: BK24 constructs partial decision functions with bounded approximate degree and two-sided conical degree O(polylog n), but Q=tildeOmega(n^(1/6)); input length is at most 2^polylog(n).

claims.statement: For every N-bit search relation S, psQ(S)=O((R(S)+V(S))*sqrt(N)).
claims.proof_summary: Use the completeness reduction to Find1 with randomized generation and deterministic verification, then apply the O(sqrt(N)) pseudo-deterministic quantum Find1 algorithm.
claims.notes: This is multivariate and input-length dependent; it is excluded from scalar exponent closure. Verification cost V can be large even for a total relation.

claims.statement: AOES is a total N-bit search relation with R=O(1) and psQ=Omega(N).
claims.proof_summary: The input hides a string through XOR blocks; any other string is a valid answer, so blind random output succeeds. A canonical solver can be amplified and converted into solving an XOR instance, giving the linear lower bound.
claims.notes: Arbitrary total relation, not a claim of a short-verification query-TFNP separation.

claims.statement: QL-Estimation has R=O(1), psQ=O(log N), and psR=Omega(sqrt(N)) in its stated mixed-oracle model. The classical algorithm that is canonized uses O(log N) queries.
claims.locator: ICALP Definition 36 and Theorem 37; introduction Theorem 3
claims.proof_summary: Use Simon’s hidden period as a key selecting a canonical approximate Hamming weight. The quantum algorithm learns the key, whereas a classical canonical solver either solves Simon or stabilizes Hamming-weight estimation.

assumptions: One query to f returns an n-bit symbol; X queries return one bit; N=2^n is a length parameter.

claims.notes: This is a promised relation with mixed alphabet queries. Bit-expanding the f oracle changes costs and must be stated explicitly.

claims.statement: On the promise |x|>=n/2, Find1 has R=O(1) and psQ=Omega(sqrt(n)); hence it separates randomized solving from quantum canonical solving.
claims.proof_summary: Show any low-query quantum canonical solver for Find1 would violate a hybrid distinguishability bound; the paper also establishes completeness for search with efficient verification.

claims.statement: For weak promise certificates, fbs(f)=FC(f)=Theta(RC(f)), including partial Boolean functions.
claims.locator: LP duality and fixed-target verifier sampling; docs/partial-functions.md
claims.proof_summary: Fractional packing/cover LP duality gives fbs=FC. Replay a verifier on the fixed target x: its probabilities of querying coordinates, doubled, cover every opposite input because rejection requires a mismatch. Conversely, sample from a fractional certificate with a constant expected number of queries per unit total weight; every opposite input is rejected with constant probability.
claims.notes: This equivalence concerns fractional weak certificates, not classical CAdv. CAdv can be much larger on promises.

claims.statement: On promise-unit-OR, D is unbounded while deg=O(1). Thus D is not O(max(1,deg)^p) for any fixed finite p over partial Boolean functions.
claims.proof_summary: Unrestricted polynomial sum_i x_i is exact and has degree one. Zero requires inspecting all coordinates classically; each unit position is a disjoint sensitive singleton at zero. The sensitivity graph is a star with norm sqrt(m). Grover search gives Q=O(sqrt(m)); the star adversary gives the matching lower bound. For exact search, apply BHMT02 Theorem 4 with hypothesized marked fraction 1/m and verify the returned index. When there is one mark it is found with certainty; when there are none verification rejects. This also proves QE=O(sqrt(m)).
claims.notes: This consequence uses weak promise certificates and unrestricted promise degree. It does not extend to globally bounded degree without a separate argument.

claims.proof_summary: There are no promised pairs at Hamming distance one, hence s=lambda=0. Substitution x_(2i-1)=x_(2i)=z_i converts any interpolating/approximating polynomial to parity on m bits, giving degree m. Flip whole pairs for bs=m. One representative bit per pair supplies the classical upper bound; standard parity lower bounds and verification give linear remaining measures.
claims.notes: This consequence uses weak promise certificates and unrestricted promise degree. It does not extend to globally bounded degree without a separate argument.

claims.proof_summary: Any two lines intersect, so bs=1. Put weight 1/(t+1) on every line to obtain fbs=Theta(t), hence RC=Theta(t). A fixed line meets all lines, so querying its t+1 points decides the problem, and yields C,D,R,R0=O(t); C,RC lower bounds give matching growth. Lines have weight t+1, so unrestricted degree is one. Promised opposite pairs are never adjacent.

claims.statement: On promise-restricted-DJ, D is unbounded while R=O(1). Thus D is not O(max(1,R)^p) for any fixed finite p over partial Boolean functions.
claims.proof_summary: The phase-query algorithm prepares the uniform state, applies phases (-1)^x_i and tests overlap with the uniform state. Its amplitude is 1 at zero and 0 on balanced inputs, hence QE=1. A weak certificate for zero needs m/2+1 zero positions, so C,D,R0=Theta(m). Random sampling gives R,RC=O(1); at zero exactly two disjoint half-size sensitive blocks can be packed, so bs=2. The promise has no opposite-output adjacent pair for m>=4. The unrestricted polynomial 2 sum_i x_i/m is exact of degree one.
claims.notes: This consequence uses weak promise certificates and unrestricted promise degree. It does not extend to globally bounded degree without a separate argument. The one-query circuit here is explicitly derived; DJ92 is the historical problem citation, not an audited original one-query attribution.

claims.statement: There are total query-TFNP relations with rel_conical=O(polylog n) but R=tildeOmega(sqrt(n)).
claims.proof_summary: The low-degree witness polynomials remain conical juntas under the total-search transformation; the shifted repeated-search quantum lower bound is unchanged. A quantum lower bound also lower-bounds classical randomized query complexity.
claims.notes: Here n is the construction parameter, not necessarily the input length. These are bounded polynomial systems and two-sided bounded conical systems.

claims.statement: AOES has R=O(1) and psR=Omega(N), as psQ<=psR.
claims.proof_summary: The input hides a string through XOR blocks; any other string is a valid answer, so blind random output succeeds. A canonical solver can be amplified and converted into solving an XOR instance, giving the linear lower bound.
claims.notes: Arbitrary total relation, not a claim of a short-verification query-TFNP separation.

claims.statement: For every total search relation, Dna(S)<=3 psRna(S).
claims.proof_summary: A coordinate with query probability below one third cannot change the canonical answer. The heavy coordinates, of which there are at most 3q, therefore determine the canonical output. Nonadaptivity makes this heavy set independent of the input.
claims.notes: The complete proof of the multi-output bound is in the ECCC report; the proceedings omits some proofs. This cubic 2023 bound predates AGL26’s discussion of an older quartic classical bound.

claims.statement: The original GGR13 theorem gives D(S)=O(psR(S)^4) for total search, with an additional output-range-sensitive bound.
claims.proof_summary: Bound the range of a canonical selector in terms of query cost, encode its outputs by bits, and deterministically compute those total Boolean bits using the classical randomized-to-deterministic simulation.
claims.notes: The complete proof of the multi-output bound is in the ECCC report; the proceedings omits some proofs. This cubic 2023 bound predates AGL26’s discussion of an older quartic classical bound.

claims.statement: Total approximate Hamming-weight search has R=O(1) and psR=Omega(n).
claims.proof_summary: Random sampling estimates normalized weight within constant additive error. Any valid selector must change between low and high weights. Follow a Hamming walk through coordinates preserving the canonical answer until this is impossible; the resulting input has linearly many sensitive coordinates, forcing linearly many randomized queries.
claims.notes: An arbitrary total relation; this is not a short-verification query-TFNP claim. GGR13 uses strict error <n/10, whereas CDM23 states the non-strict variant.

claims.statement: For total S subset {0,1}^n times [m], log DTSize(S)=O((log psDTSize(S))^4*(log n)^3*min(log m,log psDTSize(S))).
claims.proof_summary: Encode a canonical selector by output bits, bound its range using tree size, and apply the deterministic/randomized size simulation for each Boolean output bit.
claims.notes: Leaf counts, their logarithms, input length and output-range size are all explicit. This is not a quartic scalar power bound between the unlogged size measures. Final proceedings Theorem 4.3 corresponds to full-report Corollary 5.3.

claims.statement: For total approximate Hamming-weight search, RandPos=O(1) but psRandPos=Omega(n).
claims.proof_summary: Any valid selector has input-zero sensitivity Omega(n), proved by a monotone Hamming walk. The monotone block-sensitivity lower bound for randomized positive-conjunction trees then forces linearly many queries.
claims.notes: Use the Omega(n) statement. The source’s proof line claiming a stronger numerical lower bound omits the factor 1/3 from its cited corollary; no such sharpened constant is imported. Final and full-report theorem numbering differ: Theorem 5.3; full report Theorem 6.3.

claims.statement: For the total SearchOR relation, Dpar=n while psRpar=O(log n log log n), excluding every finite power upper bound on Dpar in terms of psRpar.
claims.proof_summary: On the all-zero answer path, fewer than n parity constraints leave a nonzero input in the same affine subspace as zero; the two inputs have disjoint valid outputs, so a deterministic tree cannot stop. For the canonical upper bound, binary search for the first 1, testing each half with O(log log n) random parity queries.
claims.notes: This is a parity-query separation, not a bit-query counterexample to D=O(psR^3). Final and full-report theorem numbering differ: Theorem 5.8; proof in full report Theorem 6.6.

claims.statement: For a multi-output function, mbs(f)<=3 RandPos(f) at error 1/3.
claims.proof_summary: Put half the input distribution on a target input and distribute half over disjoint sensitive zero-block flips. A positive-conjunction query can eliminate only a controlled number of these alternatives; a tree of depth below mbs/3 has distributional error greater than 1/3.
claims.notes: Here mbs is the input-zero directed block measure; it is not output-zero block sensitivity.

claims.statement: The threshold f(x)=1 iff |x|>=n-1 has RandPos=O(1) but DandPos=Omega(log n). Therefore no pure finite power of RandPos bounds DandPos for total Boolean functions.
claims.locator: Example 3.17; randomized construction in KLMY21 Example 6.3
claims.proof_summary: Split coordinates uniformly into two complementary sets and query their two conjunctions. Average the constant-size polynomials testing that all zeros lie on one side of both partitions. This is exact on positive inputs and at most 1/3 on negative inputs.

claims.statement: RC(f)<=(ln 2)*FC(f) for expected classical verification accepting the claimed input with certainty and rejecting opposite outputs with probability at least 1/2.
claims.locator: Repository elementary proof; source measure conventions
claims.proof_summary: For a fixed claimed input x, choose a fractional certificate w. Query coordinate i independently with probability 1-2^(-w_i), rejecting on disagreement. For any opposite-output y, the probability of missing every disagreement is 2^(-sum_{i:x_i!=y_i} w_i)<=1/2. The expected query count is sum_i(1-2^(-w_i))<=(ln 2)*sum_i w_i. The verifier accepts x certainly; maximize over x.
claims.notes: Repository constant refinement of fractional sampling, not a constant quoted from Aaronson. The ln 2 coefficient is asymptotically optimal for native measures over partial functions, as separately proved; sharpness for total functions or minimum-completion measures is not asserted.

claims.statement: Total address functions have nRelevant=2^k+k and UC=O(k+1), excluding every finite power.
claims.locator: Repository elementary proof; source measure conventions
claims.proof_summary: Use k address bits to select one of 2^k data bits. Every input bit is relevant, and reading the address followed by its selected data bit costs k+1. A deterministic tree supplies unambiguous certificate families from its leaves and simulates all the query measures here; fractional certificates and quantum verifiers cost at most the corresponding ordinary certificates/tree depth. Thus the right measure is at most O(k+1), while relevance is exponential in k. Total functions have a unique completion, so these witnesses lift unchanged.

claims.statement: For capped one-sided R1 with positive success at least p, D<=floor(R1/p)*C1<=R1^2/p. At p=2/3, D<=3 R1^2/2.
claims.locator: Repository certificate-query coupling proof; compare Nis89 one-sided argument and AIK26 capped convention
claims.proof_summary: Query a consistent positive certificate each round. At any surviving zero input x, replace only its disagreeing literals in each queried certificate to obtain positive inputs y_j; their disagreement blocks are nonempty and disjoint. Couple an R1 computation on x and each y_j with the same randomness. Acceptance probability at least p on y_j and no false positives on x force querying block j with probability at least p on x. Hence kp<=T. After floor(T/p) rounds a nonconstant restriction would allow one more disjoint block, impossible. Each round costs at most C1. A positive accepting transcript is a certificate of width at most T, so C1<=T.
claims.notes: R1 here is a worst-execution query cap, with no false positives. This constant is not transferred to the expected-cost Nisan convention. Constant functions use zero queries. No optimality claim for the quadratic leading constant.

claims.proof_summary: Lift f to permutations of kn vertices by grouping consecutive positions into k-sets. A permutation query or inverse query can be simulated with at most one hyperedge query by lazily assigning each newly discovered hyperedge to an unused position block. For t disjoint sensitive permutation transpositions, form a multigraph on original hyperedges. Sensitive swaps join distinct hyperedges, and each hyperedge has degree at most k because the transpositions use disjoint positions. Greedy matching gives at least t/(2k-1) swaps on disjoint hyperedge pairs, so s_perm<=(2k-1)*s_hyper. The permutation inequalities degree<=2s^2, bs<=6degree^2, C<=3s*bs and D<=2C^2 give D_perm<=10368*s_perm^10. Combine the query simulation and sensitivity comparison. The fresh source audit repairs the imported cube orientation to output/B-column transpositions; the constant survives.

formulation_audit.fixed_completion: For a fixed F extending f and a full degree-t basis, q approximates F iff Delta=coeff(q)-coeff(p) gives p_Delta=q. This is an exact representation equivalence, not a new characterization theorem.
formulation_audit.fixed_sign_completion: If F is required to equal sign(p) off the promise, existence of some other low-degree completion does not imply this fixed F is easy. Kernel preservation on the promise does not establish off-promise sign agreement.

uniformity_and_norm_audit.uniform_polynomial: A family interpretation must fix polynomial overhead constants independently of n and the particular function; allowing a different constant for every single finite function makes poly(d) vacuous.
uniformity_and_norm_audit.bounded_target_coefficients: For globally bounded p and q, each Fourier coefficient has magnitude at most one, so unrestricted Delta=qhat-phat has coefficient infinity norm at most two. Thus that norm restriction alone does not distinguish bounded target approximants in the enlarged full basis.
uniformity_and_norm_audit.exact_domain_kernel: Delta in ker(A_D) forces q=p pointwise on the promise, stronger than q merely approximating the same Boolean labels. It is not automatic for an arbitrary target approximant.
uniformity_and_norm_audit.fixed_target: For fixed F and a full permitted basis, existence of q approximating F and existence of an unrestricted coefficient perturbation yielding such q are equivalent by coefficient subtraction. clarifications.text: Definition 59 fixes F_p(x)=+1 when p(x)>=0 and -1 otherwise. Its no-blowup condition is measured against native approximate degree a. Conjecture 72 instead writes polynomial in d=deg(p). For a family, require d=poly(a) with common constants before treating these scales as interchangeable. At zeros, F_p=+1; a replacement approximant need not share those zeros.

clarifications.title: A diagnostic family for the degree mismatch
clarifications.text: On the promise product_{i=2}^n x_i=1, let f_n(x)=x_1 and choose p_n(x)=product_{i=1}^n x_i. Native approximate degree is one, but the chosen polynomial and its fixed natural completion have approximate degree n. Delta=0 satisfies the polynomial-in-d approximant condition. Thus arbitrary p and a native-degree left side cannot be combined literally; this diagnoses a missing degree hypothesis rather than refuting an intended optimal-degree version.
clarifications.proof_summary: Both labels occur on the promise, so no constant approximates f_n; x_1 does. For any polynomial r of degree less than n, orthogonality gives E[r chi_[n]]=0. Uniform approximation to chi_[n] with error below one would instead force this expectation positive. Hence the natural parity completion has approximate degree n.

clarifications.title: Literal unrestricted perturbation is an equivalence of coordinates
clarifications.text: With a full degree-t basis, t>=d, every approximant q to this same fixed F_p has Delta=qhat-phat and p_Delta=q. Conversely such a perturbation already supplies an approximant. This implication needs neither a kernel condition nor Lemma 71. It is an algebraic observation about the literal enlarged-basis statement, not evidence for a stronger restricted characterization.

clarifications.title: A precise sufficient normalization condition
clarifications.text: An editorial sufficient statement, not a replacement author conjecture: q has degree t, full-cube norm at most K, full-cube margin gamma>0 and sign(q)=F_p everywhere. Then fixed-error approximate degree of F_p is O(tK/gamma). To obtain polynomial native-degree overhead, t and K/gamma must be polynomial in a with uniform constants. Keeping only promise signs gives some completion, not necessarily F_p. A coefficient infinity-norm bound alone does not control K.
clarifications.proof_summary: Normalize by K, then compose with a polynomial sign approximant on the two intervals separated from zero by gamma/K. The unrestricted original-support dependent-kernel case remains unverified.

witnesses.definition: OR of n input bits
witnesses.parameter: n = input length
witnesses.notes: Use to witness quadratic lower exponents for D/Q, R/Q, deg/Q, and deg/adeg. Not a quartic witness.

witnesses.definition: Domain {0^m,e_1,...,e_m}; output 0 at zero and 1 on unit vectors.
witnesses.proof_summary: Unrestricted polynomial sum_i x_i is exact and has degree one. Zero requires inspecting all coordinates classically; each unit position is a disjoint sensitive singleton at zero. The sensitivity graph is a star with norm sqrt(m). Grover search gives Q=O(sqrt(m)); the star adversary gives the matching lower bound. For exact search, apply BHMT02 Theorem 4 with hypothesized marked fraction 1/m and verify the returned index. When there is one mark it is found with certainty; when there are none verification rejects. This also proves QE=O(sqrt(m)).
witnesses.parameter: m (growing positive integer)
witnesses.notes: Growth exponents are bounds in the construction parameter, not claims of optimal separation exponents in all models. A zero upper exponent denotes O(1), including zero. No original-priority claim is made for repository derivations.

witnesses.definition: Domain x_(2i-1)=x_(2i), i=1,...,m. Output parity of the m decoded bits.
witnesses.proof_summary: There are no promised pairs at Hamming distance one, hence s=lambda=0. Substitution x_(2i-1)=x_(2i)=z_i converts any interpolating/approximating polynomial to parity on m bits, giving degree m. Flip whole pairs for bs=m. One representative bit per pair supplies the classical upper bound; standard parity lower bounds and verification give linear remaining measures.
witnesses.parameter: m (growing positive integer)
witnesses.notes: Growth exponents are bounds in the construction parameter, not claims of optimal separation exponents in all models. A zero upper exponent denotes O(1), including zero. No original-priority claim is made for repository derivations.

witnesses.definition: Input (a,b) in {0,1}^{2m}. Domain: (|a|>=ceil(m/2), b=0^m) OR (a=0^m, |b|>=ceil(m/2)); output identifies the nonzero half.
witnesses.proof_summary: Each promised input has a one-bit weak certificate: any of its 1 positions identifies the half. Sampling uniformly until a 1 is found is zero-error and uses at most four queries in expectation, so R0,R,Q,RC,bs are O(1). There are no opposite-output adjacent inputs. To lower-bound exact degree, symmetrize p(a,0) and p(0,b) separately. If degree is less than floor(m/2)+1, the first univariate polynomial is identically its required constant and the second is identically the other constant, because both agree at at least floor(m/2)+1 consecutive weights. Their values at zero must agree, a contradiction. Thus deg=Omega(m), QE>=deg/2, and D>=deg. Deterministic evaluation gives O(m) upper bounds.
witnesses.parameter: m (growing positive integer)
witnesses.notes: Growth exponents are bounds in the construction parameter, not claims of optimal separation exponents in all models. A zero upper exponent denotes O(1), including zero. No original-priority claim is made for repository derivations.

witnesses.definition: Input (a,b) in {0,1}^{2m}. Domain: a nonzero and b=0^m OR a=0^m and b nonzero. Output identifies the nonzero half.
witnesses.proof_summary: Again C=RC=fbs=bs=1 and s=lambda=0. If p approximates the side label on the promise, amplify it on its two promised ranges to error 1/12 using a constant-degree polynomial. Then q(z)=p(0,z)-p(z,0), with sign chosen for the label convention, is zero at z=0 and within 1/6 of 1 for every nonzero z. It approximates total OR, so degree(p)=Omega(sqrt(m)). A bounded-error algorithm searches for a marked bit; the lower bound follows from this degree argument. Linear exact degree follows because the restrictions p(a,0) and p(0,b) would otherwise force incompatible values at their common origin.
witnesses.parameter: m (growing positive integer)
witnesses.notes: Growth exponents are bounds in the construction parameter, not claims of optimal separation exponents in all models. A zero upper exponent denotes O(1), including zero. No original-priority claim is made for repository derivations.

witnesses.definition: Domain consists of zero and the incidence vectors of lines in a projective plane of order t. Output distinguishes zero from a line. Use m=t as the growth parameter.
witnesses.locator: Theorem 17 with k=1; LP/verifier and fixed-line consequences derived here
witnesses.proof_summary: Any two lines intersect, so bs=1. Put weight 1/(t+1) on every line to obtain fbs=Theta(t), hence RC=Theta(t). A fixed line meets all lines, so querying its t+1 points decides the problem, and yields C,D,R,R0=O(t); C,RC lower bounds give matching growth. Lines have weight t+1, so unrestricted degree is one. Promised opposite pairs are never adjacent.

witnesses.notes: Growth exponents are bounds in the construction parameter, not claims of optimal separation exponents in all models. A zero upper exponent denotes O(1), including zero. No original-priority claim is made for repository derivations.

witnesses.definition: Joint truth tables f,g with forrelation exactly +1 or -1; output its sign. Parameter m=2^n; input length 2m.
witnesses.proof_summary: Use GS26 Theorem 4. Exact quantum cost is constant in standard bit-oracle conventions, while R=tildeOmega(m^(1/4)). The logarithmic loss does not affect the unboundedness consequence used here.

witnesses.definition: For even m, domain {0^m} union all strings of weight m/2. Output 0 at zero and 1 on balanced strings.
witnesses.proof_summary: The phase-query algorithm prepares the uniform state, applies phases (-1)^x_i and tests overlap with the uniform state. Its amplitude is 1 at zero and 0 on balanced inputs, hence QE=1. A weak certificate for zero needs m/2+1 zero positions, so C,D,R0=Theta(m). Random sampling gives R,RC=O(1); at zero exactly two disjoint half-size sensitive blocks can be packed, so bs=2. The promise has no opposite-output adjacent pair for m>=4. The unrestricted polynomial 2 sum_i x_i/m is exact of degree one.

witnesses.definition: Domain consists of unit vectors in {0,1}^{2m}; output whether the unique 1 lies in the first or second half.
witnesses.proof_summary: A one-bit weak certificate reads the marked position, so C=RC=fbs=bs=1. AKPVZ18 Theorem 9 uses the complete bipartite relation between the two halves to prove classical adversary Omega(m), hence R=Omega(m), and R0,D are at least as large. Scanning all coordinates gives matching upper bounds. The sum of the second-half input bits is an exact unrestricted degree-one polynomial. No two promised inputs are adjacent.

witnesses.name: OpenAI baseline
witnesses.definition: The base predicates are indicators of unions of separated Hamming balls. Recursive rows are indexed by a regular labelled tournament: each accepting clause requires strong predicates throughout its target row and weaker blocking predicates at labelled positions in outgoing rows. An OR of disjoint copies balances the two output sensitivities; disjoint self-composition amplifies the seed.
witnesses.proof_summary: Random edge labels exclude excessive simultaneous near-satisfied clauses. Four coupled profiles control ordinary sensitivity and simultaneous flips of distinct nested predicates. Block witnesses at zero multiply through recursion; OR balancing gives s<=2(d+2)M^(d+1) and bs at zero >=M^2(2M^2+1)^d for M>=9^(d+1). Composition multiplies the zero-input block lower bound and at most multiplies sensitivity.

measure_families.name: certification transform
measure_families.definition: For a measure M defined on partial Boolean functions, M^cert(f)=max_z M(f_z^cert), where f_z^cert accepts z and rejects all inputs with opposite f-value.

measure_families.name: single-bit certificate game variants
measure_families.definition: Restrict the input pairs of a certificate game to Hamming distance one; retain the randomness/resource model.

measure_families.name: noisy-oracle quantum query models
measure_families.definition: Separate measures for negligent, dephasing, and hybrid oracle access; these models are not interchangeable.

matrix_baseline_witness.locator: Section 6.2 (PARITY); elementary certificates and cube spectrum
matrix_baseline_witness.statement: For n-bit parity, each of these twelve measures is Theta(n).
matrix_baseline_witness.proof_summary: Every differing singleton is sensitive, so bs, certificate and randomized certificate costs are linear. The sensitivity graph is the n-cube, of norm n. Fourier orthogonality forces approximate degree n. The polynomial method and reading all bits sandwich the query costs.
matrix_baseline_witness.note: Establishes lower exponent 1 in every ordered core pair; it is not an upper-bound assertion.

priority_audits.finding: Use CDM23 Theorem 3.2: D=O(psR^3) for total relations. AGL26 compares its quantum result to an older quartic classical theorem; that does not supersede the cubic bound. Original GGR13 Theorem 4.1(3) was now read directly; its quartic bound has no input-length logarithm. Treat the extra logarithm in AGL26’s discussion as a weaker summary, not part of the original theorem.

AB23 separates Q from exact degree bounded on the entire cube (Boolean degree O(log N)); BK24 separates Q even from bounded approximate degree and conical degree. Neither statement is an unrestricted promise-degree result in disguise.
Four-author STACS publication and five-author arXiv v3 are separate records. Theorems 9, 15 and 17 inspected here are the v3 locators.
Final CCC Lemma 27 repairs arXiv v1: q(x,i)=q_x(i). This closes the statement/proof factor discrepancy and supports CAdv<=cfbs with constant one. Lemma 26 supplies cfbs<=2 CAdv.

The final MFCS Theorems 4.5–4.6 and 5.5–5.7 contain the ApproxMaj completion lower bound, exponential canonical-size gap and AND/OR extensions absent from the inspected earlier ECCC report. Its Theorem 4.5 expressly credits the corruption argument to Swagato Sanyal.

Replaced secondary-only use of logarithmic size derandomization by the original STOC Theorem 3.1, and original AND/OR and AND-query bounds (Theorems 4.1 and 4.5). Proposition 2.11 attributes deterministic rank-size to Ehrenfeucht–Haussler; randomized extension is syntactic.

R^{0-dt} counts zero answers, while R0 is expected zero-error cost. HSC_0/FHSC_0 refer to input-zero sensitive blocks, not output-zero certificates. Registered as separate measures / qualified aliases.

CMP22 DTSize/RDTSize count total nodes, unlike CDM23/CDMRS23 leaf size. Its randomized-relation simulation is Q_{2/5}, not default Q_{1/3}; Boolean majority reduction is only used in a decision-function record. Coupled rank/depth tree bounds are stored without multiplying separately minimized measures.

LL16 supplies the original guessing-algorithm O(sqrt(TG)) simulation and bomb-query characterization. BT20 generalizes input/output alphabets and expected random-algorithm parameters using span programs and adversary SDPs. CMP22 identifies guessing complexity with Strahler rank and optimizes edge weights to obtain the sqrt(node-size) bound.

KLMY21 bare HSC/FHSC are input-directed and match MCC/fmbs. CDMRS23 bare HSC is ordinary certificate complexity and HSC_0/FHSC_0 are the directed variants. KLMY21 also uses P^{wedge-dt}/P^{0-dt}, where later papers use D. Its Claim 4.4 reproduces the zero-depth/conjunction proof and attributes it to Loff–Mukhopadhyay 2019; the original STACS Definitions 9–10 and Lemma 11 are now inspected. Its omitted proof is supplied by KLMY21.

KLMY21 spar counts nonzero 0/1 monomials, whereas the parity-query survey uses Walsh Fourier sparsity. AND_n has monomial sparsity 1 and Fourier sparsity 2^n. A separate measure prevents transferring its hitting-set and AND-query bounds to the wrong basis.

Conjecture 3.19 says spar<=poly(approx_spar) literally. Sparse25 Remark 1.2 disproves that scale while proving a log-scale relationship with input length. Keep the negative and positive results separate.

The October 2026 revision restricts its near-half-exponent lower bound to nonadaptive algorithms and explicitly identifies the v1 gap in Appendix D. GS26 adaptive Conjecture 6 remains unresolved by this source.
